thread:
anya: Quick thread on eviction heuristics for reserved pools. We need a single prioritized algorithm that balances SLA tier, recent usage, carryover state, and fairness decay. Main ask from sales: avoid evicting premium customers during short bursts.

devon: Agreed. We should compute a real-time priority score and evict lowest score when under memory/slot pressure. Important to include a cooldown window so we don't repeatedly evict the same tenant.

priya: From billing POV, carryover debt should lower priority, but we can't just punish tenants who opt in. Maybe a small multiplier rather than absolute block.

jake: Here's a compact proposal for score (pseudocode):

```npriority = base_priority_from_SLA * SLA_WEIGHT
          - recent_cpu_percentile(5m) * USAGE_WEIGHT
          - carryover_balance * CARRYOVER_PENALTY
          + fairness_bonus(age_since_last_eviction)
```n
We can tune weights. fairness_bonus should decay exponentially so long-stable tenants get a small protection.

ron: Also add a soft-eviction phase: when pressure hits threshold X, mark candidates with a "soft_avoid" flag for N seconds and try to prewarm alternatives (route to compat model or queue) before hard eviction. That buys time for autoscale.

anya: Love the soft-evict idea. For prewarming: can we preemptively spin up a mini-pool of cheap instances for tenants crossing a usage delta? That would avoid affecting latency for short spikes.

devon: We have to watch cost. Maybe limit prewarm to sale-approved pilot customers or to pools where predicted spike looks >2x baseline and >30s duration. Predictive window can use a short AR(3) of arrival rate.

priya: And log all evictions with context to Billing/CS dashboards so we can surface customer impact. If premium tenant evicted, immediate alert to CS.

jake: UI surface: Console should show "eviction risk" score per tenant in pool and explain the top 3 contributing factors. Also an override toggle for account owners to lock for short windows.

ron: Implementation notes: exporter needs to emit: current_score, last_eviction_ts, carryover_balance, recent_p95_cpu, predicted_30s_rate. These should be 1s-granularity rollups.

devon: We need simulation before rollout. I can run a sim harness with synthetic tenants: 10% premium, 70% standard, 20% bursty. We'll measure latency delta and eviction churn under different weight sets.

anya: Rollout plan idea: (1) server-side gated feature flag, (2) enable risk scores in Console for internal view, (3) run sim + small pilot (3 tenants), (4) enable auto-evict with soft-phase for pilot customers.

priya: Decision on carryover interaction: carryover reduces score by at most 25% of base_priority (cap). That prevents outright eviction just because a tenant used carryover.

jake: Decision noted. For cooldown: don't evict the same tenant more than once per 10m unless sustained pressure > 5m.

ron: infra-bot: please create an exporter schema ticket and a sim job.

infra-bot: auto: Created tickets: EXPORTER-482 (score fields), SIM-1337 (eviction churn sim). Assigned devon and ron.

devon: Action items: (1) I'll wire the score computation into pool controller (PR by Wed) (2) run sim across weight grid and post results (due Fri).

jake: (1) I'll draft Console risk UI and override UX (due Thu) (2) add help text explaining carryover cap.

priya: I'll prepare billing/CS alert templates and escalation flow (due Thu).

anya: Good progress. We'll hold final weighting decisions after sim results. Tag me on PRs.

ron: I'll kick off the sim template today and add a synthetic workload generator for conversational long-tail patterns.

anya: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene next week to pick weights and finalize rollout gating. :shipit:
